summary: Tested promo codes (backend API plus real Stripe checkout), admin menu and promo page UI, vessel typing race fix, Terms gate spacer, Joined UTC/local times on /admin, and the scan dialog wording (by code review). Everything in scope passes. Backend pytest 17/17. Stripe hosted checkout shows 'Add promotion code'. NOTACODE99 gives 'This code is invalid.' TESTMBP25 brings the total to NZ$7.49 with '25% off for a year, then NZ$9.99 per year starting next year'. No payment was completed.

ui_bugs.issue: The input is type=number with max=100, so a value over 100 (e.g. 150) triggers the browser's own validation and blocks onSubmit. The browser tooltip shows instead of promo-error, and any earlier promo-error text (e.g. 'Pick an expiry date') stays on screen, which is misleading. Fix: add noValidate to the form, or clear the error on change.

issues: The 0-items text still says "AI couldn't spot any items in X". Consider "Magic Scan couldn't spot any items..." to match the new wording.

Expiry uses the browser's native date picker (type=date), which matches the spec but not the shadcn Calendar used elsewhere. The client error says 'between 1 and 100%' but 0.5 is accepted (step=any), which is a small mismatch.

action_items: Optional: add noValidate to promo-code-form, or clear promo-error on input change, so >100% shows the app's own error
Optional: change the empty-scan wording to Magic Scan
critical_code_review_comments: promo_codes.py: the GET list makes 2 Stripe calls (price plus all promotion codes, paged) on every page load. Fine for now, but it will slow down as codes grow.

The duplicate check is DB-only, with no unique index on promo_codes.code. A double-submit race could create 2 Stripe coupons; Stripe would reject the duplicate promotion code and the coupon gets rolled back, so the risk is low. Consider a unique index.
useBoatStore editsRef fix looks right: the PUT reply is ignored and pending stays at 1 or more when edits happen mid-flight.
